Source_Framework: MCCIP UK Marine Climate Change Impacts Evidence Hub
Units_Measure: Sea-surface and bottom temperature, °C; trend °C per decade
Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence for adaptation and marine policy: informs CCRA4-IA and the National Adaptation Programmes, and UK Marine Strategy assessments of good environmental status.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Sea Temperature topic review, update October 2025
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: sea-surface and bottom temperature — itself a physical climate-system variable. Observed: UK sea-surface temperature has warmed by around 0.3°C per decade over the last 40 years, most in the southern North Sea. Projected: Annual mean SST up to 3.11°C (±0.98°C) higher by 2079–2098 than 2000–2019 under RCP8.5; bottom temperature up to 2.49°C (±0.94°C). (Legend 3, rule E ii; aligned with [IND-B-162])

Source_Reference: MCCIP Oxygen topic review, update August 2025
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: dissolved-oxygen concentration — a physical-chemical ocean variable of the same kind as pH. Observed: Global ocean oxygen content has fallen by more than 2% since the 1960s; seasonal oxygen depletion is more frequent in the North Sea and has been detected in the Celtic Sea. Projected: UK shelf declines strongest in the North Sea and western English Channel (3–4% by 2100); about 2% in deeper regions exchanging with the open ocean. (Legend 3, rule E ii)
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Physical environment; Observed confidence: Low (low evidence, medium consensus); Projection confidence: Medium (medium evidence, medium consensus)

Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence for adaptation and marine policy: informs CCRA4-IA and the National Adaptation Programmes, and UK Marine Strategy assessments of good environmental status.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Stratification topic review (draws on Tinker et al. 2024)
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: strength and timing of thermal stratification, computed from temperature and salinity profiles — a physical ocean variable. Observed: Earlier onset of seasonal stratification in UK shelf seas, with tentative evidence of long-term strengthening; no discernible trend in coastal waters. Projected: By 2100 thermal stratification in UK shelf seas lasts about two weeks longer and is stronger, with consequences for nutrient mixing, primary production and bottom-water oxygen. (Legend 3, rule E ii)
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Physical environment; Observed confidence: Low (low evidence, medium consensus); Projection confidence: Low (low evidence, low agreement)

Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence for adaptation and marine policy: informs CCRA4-IA and the National Adaptation Programmes, and UK Marine Strategy assessments of good environmental status.
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: salinity of shelf seas and the adjacent Atlantic — a physical ocean variable. Observed: UK shelf-sea and adjacent Atlantic salinity is highly variable on annual and decadal timescales with no clear long-term trend; recent marked freshening of eastern North Atlantic waters west of the UK. Projected: Most 21st-century projections show UK shelf seas and the adjacent Atlantic becoming less saline, driven by ocean-circulation change; larger decreases in the North Sea than the Irish and Celtic Seas. (Legend 3, rule E ii)

Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence for adaptation and marine policy: informs CCRA4-IA and the National Adaptation Programmes, and UK Marine Strategy assessments of good environmental status.
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: mean sea level — itself a physical climate-system variable. Observed: Mean sea level around the UK has risen by about 12–16 cm since 1900, faster in the 20th century than the 19th. Projected: By 2100: London 0.45–0.78 m, Cardiff 0.43–0.76 m, Belfast 0.26–0.58 m, Edinburgh 0.23–0.54 m, depending on emissions scenario. (Legend 3, rule E ii; aligned with [IND-B-160])

Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence for adaptation and marine policy: informs CCRA4-IA and the National Adaptation Programmes, and UK Marine Strategy assessments of good environmental status.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Ocean Acidification topic review, update February 2025
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: seawater pH and carbonate saturation state — a physical-chemical climate variable. Observed: Atmospheric CO2 exceeded 420 ppm in 2024, rising about 2.5 ppm a year over the last decade; North Atlantic pH continues to decline. Projected: Shelf-sea pH declines at the current rate to 2050 and then faster; by 2100 up to 90% of north-west European shelf seas may be undersaturated in aragonite for at least one month a year. (Legend 3, rule E ii; aligned with [IND-B-197], [GBF-168], [SDG-128])
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Physical environment; Observed confidence: High (high evidence, high consensus); Projection confidence: Medium (medium evidence, medium agreement)

Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence for adaptation and marine policy: informs CCRA4-IA and the National Adaptation Programmes, and UK Marine Strategy assessments of good environmental status.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Ocean Circulation topic review, update September 2025
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: strength of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (Sv) — a physical climate-system variable. Observed: The AMOC strengthened in the 1990s, weakened to the early 2010s, recovered slightly, and has weakened again recently; observed trend since 2004 about −1 Sv per decade. Projected: AMOC weakening by 2100 is a robust projection, consistent in magnitude with the observed trend. (Legend 3, rule E ii)

Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence for adaptation and marine policy: informs CCRA4-IA and the National Adaptation Programmes, and UK Marine Strategy assessments of good environmental status.

Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: Arctic September sea-ice extent — a physical climate-system variable. Observed: September minimum Arctic sea-ice extent has fallen by about 79,000 km² a year since 1979, around 12% per decade relative to the 1981–2010 mean. Projected: The Arctic becomes practically ice-free at the seasonal minimum at least once before 2050 under any emissions scenario. (Legend 3, rule E ii)

Source_Framework: MCCIP UK Marine Climate Change Impacts Evidence Hub
Units_Measure: Saltmarsh extent (% change); dune and soft-cliff erosion rates
Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence on ecosystem change: informs CCRA4-IA, the UK Marine Strategy (good environmental status) and marine nature recovery.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Coastal and Intertidal Habitats topic review, update May 2026
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: saltmarsh and other coastal habitat extent, from mapping. No climate data enter it and weather does not materially move the annual value; sea level and storms are long-run drivers. Observed: Relative sea-level rise and coastal hazards are affecting saltmarshes: more erosion from stronger wave action, more frequent flooding of low marsh, and landward migration of habitats. Projected: An estimated 11% loss of UK saltmarsh by 2060 without restoration; dune erosion continues to increase; soft-cliff retreat three to seven times faster in North Devon and Yorkshire by 2100. (Legend 1, rule B; aligned with [GBF-101], [IND-S-026])
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Ecosystem change; Observed confidence: High (high evidence, high consensus — saltmarsh); Projection confidence: High (high evidence, high consensus — saltmarsh)

Indicator_Name: Shallow subtidal, shelf and deep-sea habitats
Source_Framework: MCCIP UK Marine Climate Change Impacts Evidence Hub
Units_Measure: Benthic community composition and species distributions; kelp assemblages; seafloor biomass (%)
Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence on ecosystem change: informs CCRA4-IA, the UK Marine Strategy (good environmental status) and marine nature recovery.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Shallow Subtidal, Shelf and Deep-sea Habitats topic review, update June 2026
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: benthic community composition, species distributions and kelp assemblages, from field survey. No climate data enter the measures and they integrate change over years rather than responding materially to a single year's weather; ocean warming is the recognised long-run driver. Projections use habitat-suitability modelling with climate data, but the observed measures do not. Observed: North Sea infaunal species have shifted distribution with warming but most cannot keep pace; UK kelp assemblages have changed; plankton changes are reducing organic carbon flux to the seabed; deep-sea sponge communities show resilience. Projected: Significant kelp range shifts by 2050; restructured North Sea benthic communities by 2100; only 30–42% of present habitat for the reef-forming coral Desmophyllum pertusum persisting as refugia; global seafloor biomass down 3% by 2050 and 5.9% by 2080. (Legend 1, rule B)
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Ecosystem change; Observed confidence: Low (shelf: medium evidence, low consensus; deep sea: low evidence, medium consensus); Projection confidence: Low (shelf and deep sea)

Source_Framework: MCCIP UK Marine Climate Change Impacts Evidence Hub
Units_Measure: Plankton biomass and community composition (size classes); bloom timing; distribution shifts
Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence on ecosystem change: informs CCRA4-IA, the UK Marine Strategy (good environmental status) and marine nature recovery.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Plankton and Pelagic Habitats topic review, update 2026
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: plankton biomass, community composition and bloom timing from long-term survey and monitoring. Inter-annual sea temperature and stratification move the values materially; climate data are not an input to the indices. Observed: Large phyto- and zooplankton are declining in oceanic waters beyond the shelf, while smaller plankton and microbial species dominate in warmer, stratified shelf waters. Projected: Earlier and longer spring blooms in some regions, further northward shifts of plankton and fish, reduced overall primary productivity and more dominance by smaller phytoplankton. (Legend 2, rule D; aligned with [GBF-111])
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Ecosystem change; Observed confidence: Medium (high evidence, medium consensus); Projection confidence: Medium (medium evidence, low consensus)

Source_Framework: MCCIP UK Marine Climate Change Impacts Evidence Hub
Units_Measure: Species distribution and abundance; habitat suitability; thermal thresholds (°C)
Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence on ecosystem change: informs CCRA4-IA, the UK Marine Strategy (good environmental status) and marine nature recovery.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Fish topic review (Wright et al. 2020, updated 2023)
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: fish distribution, abundance and stock status from surveys and stock assessments, in which sea temperature enters productivity and recruitment models indirectly. Observed: Warm-water fish species continue to increase in UK waters, with local declines of some cold-affinity species; several cephalopods have increased in abundance and range; Atlantic cod reproductive success falls above 9.6°C. Projected: Continued warming changes species composition in shallow areas such as the southern North Sea; by 2100 conditions may suit Mediterranean horse mackerel and bogue as far north as the mid Irish and North Seas; cod habitat shifts north. (Legend 2, rule D; aligned with [IND-E-024], [IND-C-115], [IND-B-129])
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Ecosystem change; Observed confidence: Medium (high evidence, medium agreement); Projection confidence: Medium (medium evidence, medium agreement)

Source_Framework: MCCIP UK Marine Climate Change Impacts Evidence Hub
Units_Measure: Population indices; breeding numbers and distribution; productivity and survival
Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence on ecosystem change: informs CCRA4-IA, the UK Marine Strategy (good environmental status) and marine nature recovery.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Seabirds and Waterbirds topic review (2023)
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: seabird and waterbird population indices. The seabird component alone would score 2 (survey index moved by weather, [IND-J-011]); the wintering-waterbird component is analysed with cold-weather movements in mind and scores 3 ([IND-J-013]). Waterbirds are a named part of the measure, so the climate-defined component governs. Observed: UK and Ireland seabird and waterbird indices have declined since the 1990s, linked to climate-driven changes in fish prey and to extreme weather affecting breeding success. Projected: Mixed impacts on breeding and non-breeding numbers; Arctic and sub-Arctic waterbirds wintering in the UK and Ireland are particularly vulnerable; many UK seabird populations lack resilience. (Legend 3, rules F and G; aligned with [IND-J-013]; seabird component as [IND-J-011])
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Ecosystem change; Observed confidence: Medium (medium evidence, medium agreement); Projection confidence: Low (low evidence, low agreement)

Source_Framework: MCCIP UK Marine Climate Change Impacts Evidence Hub
Units_Measure: Range and distribution shifts; disease prevalence; habitat suitability (largely qualitative)
Policy_Goal: UK marine climate evidence on ecosystem change: informs CCRA4-IA, the UK Marine Strategy (good environmental status) and marine nature recovery.
Source_Reference: MCCIP Climate Change Impacts on Marine Mammals around the UK and Ireland topic review (2023)
Data_Source: MCCIP evidence synthesis of published observations and model studies (topic review; Impacts Hub)
Climate_Rationale: Measured quantity: marine-mammal distribution and range shifts, from surveys and sightings; inter-annual ocean conditions and prey move distribution materially; no climate data enter the measures. Observed: Apparent northward shift of some warmer-water cetaceans around the UK; range shifts, habitat loss, food-web change and more disease are documented. Projected: Species tied to breeding grounds face habitat and behavioural change; disease and thermal stress may increase; breeding timing may shift. (Legend 2, rule D; aligned with [IND-E-017]; differs from [IND-S-007] cetacean abundance index, an effort-corrected abundance measure scored 1)
Framework_Classification: Role: Evidence review; Group: Ecosystem change; Observed confidence: Medium (medium evidence, medium consensus); Projection confidence: Medium (low evidence, medium consensus)
